basic_identification.full_title: HOROLOGY — WATCH BEZEL AND BACK COVER GAUGES — TECHNICAL SUPPLY CONDITIONS — GENERAL
basic_identification.sector_category: Horology Sectional Committee, LM 23 / Light Mechanical Engineering Division Council [1]

scope.summary: This Standard mainly covers the general technical supply conditions of plain and thread gauges to be used in manufacturing of watch bezels and back covers. It also recommends the material to be used in manufacturing and the markings to be provided on the gauges [2].

requirements.detail: Requires materials from IS 4432 : 1988 for manufacturing snap gauges, recommending chemical steel designations: 16 Mn 5 Cr 4 and 20 Mn 5 Cr 5 (typographically printed as 20Mn5CrS) [4].
The measuring surfaces of all manufactured gauges must carry a minimum hardness of 700 HV (equivalent to approximately 60 HRC) to prevent measurement face wear [4].
All completed gauges and gauge members must be thoroughly demagnetised after heat treatment to prevent magnetic attraction of debris [4].

Gauges and gauge members must be well-finished. All sharp corners and edges of measuring surfaces must be broken and free from burrs and defects. In thread gauges, incomplete starting threads must be removed and a blunt start provided [4].
Whenever grooves or recesses are provided on the gauges for colour coding, they must hold a minimum depth of 0.3 mm and a minimum width of 2 mm, with their bottom corners suitably rounded [4].
A suitable anti-corrosive coating must be applied on the finished gauges. They must then be wrapped in wax paper and packed inside cardboard, wooden, or plastic boxes [4].
Any final observed or calculated test or analysis value must be rounded off per IS 2 : 1960 to the same number of significant places as specified in the standard [5].

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 14339 : 1996 is the national Indian Standard specification governing general technical supply conditions for plain and thread gauges used in manufacturing watch bezels and back covers [1, 2]. Reaffirmed in 2012, this standard is finalized by the Horology Sectional Committee (LM 23) and operates as a necessary adjunct to IS 14365 : 1996, which specifies dimensional limits and tolerances [1, 2]. To maintain high accuracy and prevent measurement face wear, it mandates that measuring surfaces achieve a minimum hardness of 700 HV (60 HRC) and recommends tool steels (such as XT 215 Cr 12) or case hardening steels [3, 4]. Additionally, the standard enforces demagnetisation, deburring of sharp edges, blunt starts on threads, and outlines strict color coding and marking schemes (such as red paint identifiers on 'NOT GO' gauges) [4].
